args.title: stipulation-markup-analysis.docx
args.body:
STIPULATION MARKUP ANALYSIS
Prioritized Issues Memorandum with Recommendations
Matter: Carried Interest Tax Court Dispute — Proposed Stipulation of Facts
Counterparty: Internal Revenue Service
Output: stipulation-markup-analysis.docx
Practice Area: Tax

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

This memorandum analyzes the IRS’s markup of our proposed Stipulation of Facts against the firm’s base materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits that qualify those materials, and the controlling deal-team instruction on negotiation priorities. It identifies every material deviation introduced by the counterparty markup, reconciles each deviation against the schedules and exhibits, and assigns a priority and recommendation.

Sources relied upon (operative only):
• Base deal materials — Proposed Stipulation of Facts and firm-standard supporting provisions (Matter File 24)
• IRS / counterparty markup (counterparty markup record)
• Schedules and exhibits qualifying the base materials (Schedule 3.7; Schedule 5.2; Exhibit B)
• Controlling deal-team correspondence (latest partner instruction on concede / walk-away priorities)

Excluded: Misfiled administrative correspondence from an unrelated engagement present in the matter folder. That file was not used.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
II. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The IRS markup accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three interrelated deviations:

  (1) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap, together with conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar) basket;
  (2) Expansion of the Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition with carve-outs for regulatory action of the type at issue in this carried-interest dispute; and
  (3) A new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations, in direct conflict with the survival matrix in Exhibit B.

When read together with the schedules, these deviations are more consequential than they appear on the face of the markup alone:
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that sit squarely inside the new MAE carve-outs.
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the indemnification-cap and basket changes would silently reallocate.
  • Exhibit B’s survival matrix is contradicted by the shortened limitation period; under the schedules’ control rule, the scheduled survival terms control over general statements in the base materials and must not be diluted by the markup.

Controlling client / partner instruction (latest message only): the client will concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping) but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and are not followed here.

Priority ranking used in this memo:
  P1 — Walk-away / non-negotiable under controlling instruction
  P2 — High: material risk shift requiring reject or substantial counter
  P3 — Medium-High: economic allocation requiring restoration or express pricing
  P4 — Concede per controlling instruction (with documentation)

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
III. DEVIATION-BY-DEVIATION RECONCILIATION
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

DEVIATION A — Survival / Limitation Period Shortening for Core Representations
Priority: P1 — WALK-AWAY
Markup change: The IRS inserts a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations relative to the firm’s proposed stipulation and supporting framework.
Reconciliation to schedules/exhibits:
  • Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the core representations. The markup’s shortened limitation period directly contradicts that matrix.
  • Under the governing schedules rule, scheduled exceptions and matrices control over general statements in the base tax materials. The Exhibit B survival periods therefore control and cannot be overridden by a silent or generalized limitation-period insert in the markup.
  • Shortened survival for core representations in a carried-interest Tax Court stipulation impairs the client’s ability to rely on stipulated facts through the full litigation and any related collection, appeal, or collateral proceedings contemplated by the base materials.
Interaction with other deviations: A shortened survival window compounds Deviation B (MAE carve-outs) and Deviation C (indemnification economics): if core tax and structural representations expire early, the client bears residual risk on items the schedules already flag as live (pending regulatory inquiries; retained liabilities).
Controlling instruction: Any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue.
Recommendation:
  • REJECT the shortened limitation period in full.
  • RESTORE Exhibit B survival matrix verbatim for all core representations (and any stipulated facts that functionally operate as core reps for purposes of the stipulation).
  • Do not accept “middle-ground” partial shortening; the controlling instruction does not authorize compromise on survival.
  • If the IRS insists, escalate as a deal-breaker / stipulation-breaker under the partner instruction; do not trade survival for concessions on basket or cap without a fresh client mandate.
  • Confirm in the revised draft that Exhibit B is incorporated by reference and controls in the event of conflict.

DEVIATION B — Material Adverse Effect Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action
Priority: P2 — HIGH (Reject / Counter)
Markup change: The MAE definition is revised to add carve-outs for regulatory action “of exactly the kind at issue in this matter” (i.e., tax / carried-interest regulatory and enforcement activity).
Reconciliation to schedules/exhibits:
  • Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these MAE carve-outs. If regulatory action of this kind is carved out of MAE, those scheduled inquiries—and any escalation of them—cannot support an MAE-based right, condition, or stipulated consequence that the base materials contemplated.
  • Because scheduled exceptions control over general base-material statements, Schedule 3.7’s disclosure does not neutralize the carve-out; it identifies the precise risk the carve-out would remove from the MAE construct. The carve-out therefore silently nullifies MAE protection for the very facts the parties have already put on the schedule.
Risk assessment: In a carried-interest Tax Court dispute, regulatory action is not a theoretical tail risk; it is the subject matter. Carving it out of MAE (or from any MAE-linked stipulated predicate) is a structural reallocation of litigation and economic risk to the client.
Recommendation:
  • REJECT the regulatory-action MAE carve-outs as drafted.
  • COUNTER with one of the following (in descending order of preference):
      (1) Delete the regulatory carve-outs entirely and retain the firm’s MAE formulation;
      (2) Narrow any regulatory carve-out so that it does not reach the categories of inquiry disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and expressly preserve MAE treatment for those scheduled matters and their natural outgrowths;
      (3) If any limited regulatory carve-out is commercially forced, pair it with (a) an express stipulation that Schedule 3.7 matters remain MAE-eligible, and (b) a separate termination / re-opener or stipulated remedy tied to adverse developments on those inquiries.
  • Require the IRS to identify with specificity which “regulatory actions” it seeks to exclude, and map each against Schedule 3.7 before any language is accepted.
  • Ensure the stipulation’s factual recitals regarding the pending inquiries are not undermined by definitional carve-outs elsewhere in the package.

DEVIATION C — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
Priority: Split treatment under controlling instruction
  C.1 Basket conversion (deductible → tipping): P4 — CONCEDE
  C.2 Silent indemnification cap reduction: P3 — MEDIUM-HIGH (Reject silent cut; restore or re-price)

Markup change:
  • The indemnification basket is converted from a deductible basket to a tipping (first-dollar once threshold is met) basket.
  • The indemnification cap is silently reduced (no conspicuous call-out in the markup narrative; amount reduced relative to the firm base).

Reconciliation to schedules/exhibits:
  • Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup’s indemnification changes would silently shift. A lower cap, combined with a tipping basket, changes both when dollars begin to move and the ceiling on recovery. For retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2, that shift can move economic exposure onto the client without an express negotiation of those line items.
  • Scheduled exceptions control: Schedule 5.2’s retained-liability list must be read together with any indemnification economics. Accepting a silent cap cut without re-running Schedule 5.2 allocation is inconsistent with the schedules’ primacy.

C.1 — Basket conversion (controlling instruction: concede)
Recommendation:
  • ACCEPT conversion from deductible to tipping basket, per the latest partner / client instruction.
  • Document the concession expressly in the issues list and in the cover note to the IRS so it is credited in the overall package and not treated as unnoticed.
  • Confirm drafting: tipping mechanics (threshold amount, what counts toward the threshold, whether defense costs count, single vs. aggregate) should be stated cleanly so the concession does not create secondary ambiguity.
  • Do not allow the basket concession to be packaged as consideration for the survival cut (Deviation A) or for the MAE carve-outs (Deviation B).

C.2 — Indemnification cap reduction
Recommendation:
  • REJECT the silent cap reduction.
  • RESTORE the firm-base indemnification cap.
  • Reconcile against Schedule 5.2 line by line: any accepted change to the cap must be accompanied by an express statement of which Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain covered, which are capped, and which (if any) are excluded—so there is no silent shift.
  • If a lower cap is later authorized commercially, require (a) a visible redline and quantum, (b) Schedule 5.2 true-up, and (c) client sign-off separate from the already-authorized basket concession.
  • Flag for billing / reserve analysis: quantify the delta between firm-base cap and IRS-reduced cap against Schedule 5.2 exposure before any counter-offer on quantum.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
IV. CROSS-CUTTING RECONCILIATION NOTES
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Schedules control. Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B qualify and, where conflicting, control over general statements in the base materials. Every markup edit that touches MAE, indemnification, or survival must be tested against those schedules/exhibits—not only against the clean base text.

2. “Silent” changes. The cap reduction is described as silent. Silent economic cuts in a stipulation package used in Tax Court should be treated as high-process-risk: reverse the silence in our response (express call-out, quantum comparison, Schedule 5.2 bridge) even where we may later move on quantum.

3. No reliance on superseded priorities. Earlier deal-team messages that inverted the basket vs. survival priority are superseded. This memo follows only the latest instruction: concede basket conversion; walk away on survival reduction.

4. Misfiled materials. Unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in this matter folder was disregarded in full.

5. Stipulation-of-facts context. Although several deviations are framed in M&A-style vocabulary (MAE, indemnification, survival), they operate here inside a Proposed Stipulation of Facts in a carried-interest Tax Court dispute. Recommendations above should be implemented in the stipulation’s definitions, stipulated remedies / reservation-of-rights provisions, and any incorporated schedules/exhibits, not solely in a separate purchase agreement construct.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
V. PRIORITIZED ISSUES TABLE
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

| Pri | Issue | Markup Deviation | Schedule / Exhibit Overlay | Client Posture | Recommendation |
|-----|-------|------------------|----------------------------|----------------|----------------|
| P1  | Survival of core representations | New limitation period shortens survival | Exhibit B survival matrix contradicted; schedules control | Walk-away | Reject; restore Exhibit B in full; no partial shorten |
| P2  | MAE definition — regulatory carve-outs | Carve-outs for regulatory action of the kind at issue | Schedule 3.7: two pending regulatory inquiries intersect carve-outs | Protect MAE for scheduled matters | Reject as drafted; counter to preserve Schedule 3.7 matters; require IRS specificity |
| P3  | Indemnification cap | Silent reduction of cap | Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities would silently shift | Not authorized to concede | Reject silent cut; restore base cap; Schedule 5.2 true-up before any quantum move |
| P4  | Indemnification basket | Deductible → tipping basket | Interacts with Schedule 5.2 economics but expressly conceded | Concede | Accept tipping basket; document concession; isolate from P1–P3 trades |

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VI. RECOMMENDED RESPONSE PACKAGE
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Cover note to IRS counsel
   • Acknowledge acceptance of most firm-standard provisions.
   • Expressly concede basket conversion (deductible → tipping) and describe tipping mechanics.
   • Identify as non-acceptable: (i) any shortening of survival / limitation periods relative to Exhibit B; (ii) MAE regulatory carve-outs that reach Schedule 3.7 matters; (iii) silent reduction of the indemnification cap without Schedule 5.2 reconciliation.

2. Revised draft stipulation
   • Restore Exhibit B survival matrix; add conflict rule: Exhibit B controls.
   • Delete or tightly narrow MAE regulatory carve-outs; lock Schedule 3.7 matters into MAE-eligible treatment.
   • Restore indemnification cap to firm base; implement tipping basket per concession; attach Schedule 5.2 bridge.

3. Internal next steps
   • Partner confirmation that walk-away on survival remains current.
   • Quantitative comparison of cap delta vs. Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.
   • No further concessions on P1–P3 without written client authority.
   • File this memorandum as the operative issues list for the stipulation negotiation.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
VII. CONCLUSION
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Three markup deviations require action; the schedules and Exhibit B make each more significant than a face-value redline review would suggest. Under the controlling deal-team instruction, concede only the basket conversion. Reject and restore on survival (walk-away), reject or substantially counter on MAE regulatory carve-outs in light of Schedule 3.7, and reject the silent indemnification cap cut pending a Schedule 5.2 true-up. Implement the revised package with an express conflict rule favoring Exhibit B and the disclosure schedules.

— End of Memorandum —
